title: David Goggins on the calloused mind, the cookie jar, and doing what sucks daily
summary: Goggins tells how a cracked, abusive childhood and a victim mentality led him to build a calloused mind through relentless work. He explains the cookie jar, the "what if" mentality, tripling down on weaknesses, and why self-talk only works when backed by real work.

principles.text: Mental toughness isn't enough; build a calloused mind to escape a victim mentality.
principles.quote: mental toughness wasn't enough I had to really develop a calloused mind so I was a victim mentality

principles.text: The cookie jar: recall everything you've overcome when your mind says quit.
principles.quote: you take one second when you're an extreme environment and your mind and your body are saying we're done we need to quit you can't remind yourself hang on a second I've overcome a hell of a lot more than this

principles.text: Turn "you can't" into "but what if I could" and use doubters' negativity as fuel.
principles.quote: I got in my truck and I said to myself but what if I could what if I could pull off this miracle

principles.text: Do something every day that sucks; triple down on weaknesses, not strengths.
principles.quote: do something every day that sucks get outside your comfort zone triple down on your weaknesses not your strengths that's how you grow

principles.text: Self-talk is only true if backed by the work you've put in.
principles.quote: self talk without the work without the work it's just lies

principles.text: Be a practitioner, not a theorist; dive into suffering to learn what you're capable of.
principles.quote: you have to be willing to suffer to get to the other side you know the other side of suffering is a whole nother world
